'''Henry Ellenson''' (born January 13, 1997<ref name="USAB Bio" />) is an American [[basketball]] player who played for [[Marquette University]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Hunt|first1=Michael|title=Golden Eagles land top-10 basketball recruit Henry Ellenson|url=http://www.jsonline.com/sports/goldeneagles/golden-eagles-land-top-10-basketball-recruit-henry-ellenson-b99368024z1-278753041.html|website=Milwaukee-Wisconsin Journal Sentinel|publisher=Journal Sentinel|accessdate=28 December 2014|date=9 October 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Gruman|first1=Andrew|title=Marquette top recruit Ellenson wants to make 'big statement right away'|url=http://www.foxsports.com/wisconsin/story/marquette-top-recruit-ellenson-wants-to-make-big-statement-right-away-111214|website=FOX Sports Wisconsin|publisher=Fox Sports Interactive Media|accessdate=28 December 2014|date=12 November 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Henry Ellenson - Basketball Recruiting Player Profiles|url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/143158/Henry-Ellenson|website=ESPN.com|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|accessdate=28 December 2014|date=12 November 2014}}</ref> He was born in [[Rice Lake, Wisconsin]] and attended [[Rice Lake High School]].

==High school career==
Ellenson played basketball at Rice Lake High School, where he also competed in [[track and field]] ([[high jump]], [[discus]]).<ref name="USAB Bio">{{cite web|title=Henry Ellenson|url=http://archive.usab.com/bios/ellenson_henry.html|website=USA Basketball|publisher=NBA Media Ventures|accessdate=28 December 2014|date=18 August 2014}}</ref> In August 2014, Ellenson was a member of the United States' National Team at the [[2014 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] in [[Dubai]], scoring 21 points in the quarterfinal game with China.<ref>{{cite web|title=Henry Ellenson leads US to FIBA U17 World Championship semifinals|url=http://www.foxnews.com/sports/2014/08/14/henry-ellenson-leads-us-to-fiba-u17-world-championship-semifinals/|website=FOX News|publisher=Associated Press|accessdate=28 December 2014|date=14 August 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2014 USA Basketball Junior National Team Mini-Camp Roster|url=http://www.usab.com/mens/u16/roster.aspx|website=USA Basketball|accessdate=28 December 2014}}</ref>

During his freshman year (2011-12), Ellenson averaged 12.0 ppg., 7.0 rpg., 1.5 apg. and 1.5 bpg. The next year (2012-2013), sophomore Ellenson averaged 21.5 ppg., 11.8 rpg., 3.5 apg. and 1.8 bpg.<ref name="USAB Bio" />

===Career highlights and awards===
* Ellenson scored a career-high 48 points against Minnetonka High School on 12/6/14.
* 2013 [[MaxPreps]] Sophomore All-America honorable mention.
* 2013 Wisconsin Basketball Coaches Association Division 2 All-State first team.
* 2013 Associated Press All-State second team.
* 2013 Eau Claire Leader-Telegram Northwest Wisconsin Player of the Year, first sophomore to win the award.
* 2013 Eau Claire Leader-Telegram All-Northwest first team,
* 2013 [[St. Paul Pioneer Press]] East Metro Player of the Year.
* 2013 [[Big Rivers Conference]] Player of the Year and All-Big Rivers first team.
* 2012 All-Big Rivers Conference.

==College career==
During his only season at Marquette, Ellenson would record a near-double-double average of 17 points and 9.7 rebounds per game with 1.8 assists and 1.5 blocks recorded under 33.5 minutes of action for 33 games. As a result of his performances, he'd earn All-Big East First Team, Big East All-Freshmen Team, and Big East Freshman of the Year honors. At the conclusion of the 2015-16 regular season, he was selected to the First Team All-Big East.<ref>{{cite news|title=Four Named Unanimously to MBB All-BIG EAST First Team|url=http://www.bigeast.com/news/2016/3/6/MBB_0306160917.aspx|accessdate=March 9, 2015|work=[[Big East Conference]]|date=March 6, 2015}}</ref> After the season, he declared for the [[2016 NBA Draft]].<ref>http://www.jsonline.com/blogs/sports/374670131.html</ref>
